extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners seeking expedited examination at the USPTO (utility and plant applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for requesting USPTO Track One prioritized examination to obtain a final disposition within about 12 months for utility and plant patent applications, including eligibility, fees, filing, and procedural limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final disposition timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Track One prioritized examination allows applicants to get a final disposition within about twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY 2023 average final disposition was just over 5 months (vs. ~25 months for standard applications). Timeline expectation: target is ~12 months; actual times may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Available for utility and plant patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track One is available for an original utility or plant application at the time of filing, and is also available for Continuing Applications (continuations and divisionals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment requirement and amounts (2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Track One prioritized examination fee must be paid at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard fee: $4,200.00. Small entity: $1,680. Micro entity: $840. Fee must be submitted at filing to obtain Track One status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim count limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Application limited to 4 independent claims and 30 total claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain compliance with these claim limits to remain eligible for prioritized examination; exceeding limits may render the application ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Track One requests must be filed electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be filed through the USPTO Patent Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual cap and allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an annual limit on the number of Track One requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning July 8, 2025 the USPTO increased the annual limit from 15,000 to 20,000 per fiscal year. Program allotment is handled on a first-come, first-served basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-come, first-served availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting of Track One status is on a first-come, first-served basis within the annual cap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit early in the fiscal year to improve chances of securing one of the limited slots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of extensions of time on eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for an extension of time causes ineligibility for prioritized examination treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes extensions for responding to a pre-examination notice. Additionally, requesting an extension of time prior to the grant of prioritized examination status will prevent such status from being granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time limits and prosecution behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must respond promptly to office actions and avoid actions that delay prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extensions are permitted for responses while under Track One. Applicants should avoid practices that would delay prosecution and should maintain compliance with claim count limits to preserve prioritized status.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE single-request allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: A single Track One request may also be granted for a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) in a plant or utility application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits limited prioritized treatment post-issue of an office action via an RCE request, subject to the program rules and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended strategic use cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations in which Track One is particularly advisable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Track One for time-sensitive technology, imminent product launches, investor due diligence needs, threats of competitor entry, or technologies with short commercial life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to other acceleration options
rubrics_metrics.description: How Track One compares to other USPTO acceleration programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary table: Track One (~$4,200) requires <30 claims and disallows extensions with ~12-month timeline; Accelerated Examination (low fee) requires a pre-examination search and statement; PPH relies on allowable claims in another office; Petition to Make Special requires specific reasons (e.g., age/health); First Action Interview Pilot accelerates first action if interview occurs within 60 days of FAOM. Use these differences to choose the appropriate acceleration path.
